# Upstream books

This series is original. It does not include the text of the books below. Read them beside the volumes that point at them. Keep their licenses attached to their files if you keep your own copies.

| Work | Read it for | License constraint |
|---|---|---|
| Harvard CS249r, *Machine Learning Systems*, Volumes I–IV, [mlsysbook.ai](https://mlsysbook.ai) | Systems from one machine through scale, agents, and physical AI. Deeper than Volume 15. | Textbook text is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Share it unmodified. Do not edit it into these chapters. |
| *Dive into Deep Learning*, [d2l.ai](https://d2l.ai) | A full implemented deep-learning course. | Text is CC BY-SA 4.0. Adaptation carries attribution and share-alike. Not copied here. |
| Allen Downey, *Think Python*, *Think Stats*, *Think Bayes* | Computational introductions to Python, statistics, and Bayesian updating. | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Non-commercial adaptation is share-alike. |
| Hugging Face course, [huggingface.co/course](https://huggingface.co/course) | A library-centered course on transformers. | Apache 2.0. Reuse requires attribution, the license notice, and a note of changes. |

A free PDF is not the same thing as one of these licenses. Books you may read online and may not republish include, among others, *Understanding Deep Learning* (CC BY-NC-ND), and classic texts that are free to read but all rights reserved. Do not paste them into this repository.

Volume 18 has a chapter on how to write a reading note in your own words. Use that note instead of a close paraphrase.

## Where they sit on the path

| After you can do | Read |
|---|---|
| Volumes 01–03 | Think Python and Think Stats, if the code and the statistics still feel thin. |
| Volumes 04–05 | Think Bayes for a computational Bayesian companion. |
| Volumes 09–13 | Dive into Deep Learning, as a broader implemented course than these notes. |
| Volume 12 | The Hugging Face course, if you want the library path. Keep this volume's baselines. |
| Volume 15 and beyond | CS249r Volumes I–IV, unmodified, for hardware, scale, and the rest of the systems curriculum. |
